| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | in-progress | 2026-08-12 — library-matching moved to done — the match rung is load-bearing, landed as one OpenSpec change in five separately-green strands. D36's flip: the label predicate's set builds from component matchLabels (new schema.MatchLabels path constant) at the two matching sites; the two non-matching readers stay on metadata.labels exactly per the site table — the transformer context (pinned by a new must-not-flip test asserting matchLabels never reaches #componentMetadata) and the display-only ComponentSummary; fixtures moved to the flipped vocabulary (registrytest primitives emit matchLabels beside the transitional metadata.labels duplicate; raw compile and kernel fixtures author component matchLabels; a new case pins that metadata.labels alone no longer matches) and the forced GHCR flow test proves the flip against published catalog bytes. D28+D4: every declared resource is a required demand — empty-bucket and all-candidates-disqualified states surface as the new value-typed oerrors.UnresolvedDemand (Component, FQN, Kind, ladder-ordered Alternatives carrying the D4 different-apiVersion diagnostic, Disqualified carrying the recorded UnifyErrors, plus an UnstatedPosture marker) aggregated by *UnresolvedDemandsError (Unwrap []error); Plan/Compile fail through one exit path beside UnmatchedComponentsError (both reported when both apply, errors.Join'd); Match stays phase-only; unhandled traits follow the effective optional read off the attachment (default-resolved), non-concrete fails closed naming the unstated posture, and Warnings() carries only effectively-optional unhandled traits; plan.Missing stays fed for compatibility. D34/D4: sortFQNsBySemVer renamed to sortContractKeys, delegating to compat.CompareAPIVersions with a lexical tie-break — the measured pathological triple (v1alpha1, v2, v10) now sorts identically from every input permutation, pinned; the Masterminds semver import left the matcher (no match site orders build keys). D32/D37: the single-provider guard runs in indexCatalogs' existing walk — declared fulfilment read (default-resolved) off every REQUIRED embedded copy, provider-fulfilled keys accumulate owning subscriptions structurally, two catalogs for one key refuse materialization naming both paths and the key, divergent fulfilment for one key refuses as a divergent contract, same-catalog plurality and catalog-fulfilled plurality stay legal. D10: the own-graph gate is TestFlow_OwnGraphResolution — the platform subscribes a catalog build divergent from the module's own dependency at a shared contract key; the unify rung must report the divergence (one value under a shared resolution could never conflict with itself) and a render default stated only by the module-side build must reach compiled output. ONE RECORDED MECHANISM DEVIATION (D26/D30): the unify rung does NOT apply compat.StripProvenance — measured at implementation, the strip's Syntax(cue.All(), InlineImports(true)) round-trip cannot rebuild kernel-side schema-derived operands (let-bound references to core helper definitions like #KebabToPascal fail resolution on rebuild, against both the real GHCR catalog and registrytest fixtures), and every export profile that does rebuild them (Eval-first, cue.Final) was measured to OPEN closed definitions, silently voiding the D27 closed-definition comparison. The rung instead excludes provenance-LOCATED diagnostics (metadata.catalogVersion/description directly under any metadata block, any depth) from the unify verdict and the recorded cause — equivalent under D25 (nothing derives from the denylisted fields), closedness preserved trivially, and D30's accepted position-loss cost REVERSED: surviving diagnostics keep document positions. compat.StripProvenance itself is untouched (the publish-side gate's operands export self-contained). SECOND MEASURED FINDING, recorded in the own-graph test: unifying two INDEPENDENTLY-LOADED closed #Resource instances whose spec bodies are both nested struct literals trips a v0.17 evaluator closedness quirk (spurious 'spec.<name>: field not allowed' naming both operands' declarations — adjacent to the documented alpha.2 regression), so the gate's platform-side embedded copies keep spec bodies at underscore or a scalar; a same-key cross-build unify of struct-literal specs in production catalogs would hit the same wall, which the interim duplicate-authoring in catalog_opm avoids today. CATALOG FOLLOW-ON (owed by catalog_opm, not this slice): the transitional duplicate metadata.labels on matching-relevant PRIMITIVES is droppable once this ships — component-side metadata.labels stays meaningful for render reads (hpa_transformer's workload-type lookup) — and the D36 opm.opmodel.dev/workload-type key rename remains unlanded catalog-side (the flip here is key-neutral). MIGRATIONS.md carries the five-bullet Unreleased-Breaking entry; add-migration-guard is not live, so the PR carries no Migration: trailer. | Module and Catalog Identity |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |
| [0016](./0016/) | cli | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-13 — Drafted. Nothing turns a published module into the on-disk instance package everything downstream consumes (opm instance build/apply, the operator's ModulePackage path): `opm module init` scaffolds author-side modules, and library synth.Instance builds instances only in memory — explicitly refusing a debugValues fallback as "a frontend policy concern". Three decisions came from the user on the day: a new CLI command scaffolds a standalone instance package from an OCI module reference and tag (D1); the generated values.cue defaults to the module's debugValues, making init useful against the already-published fleet with no republish (D2); and #Module gains an optional field (working name initValues) carrying the author-intended init template, taking precedence over debugValues, whose testing contract stays unchanged (D3). Six Open Questions carried: field name/shape and #config conformance (OQ1), command surface and ref syntax (OQ2), empty-source behavior (OQ3), renderer home library-vs-cli (OQ4), init-time validation (OQ5), generated cue.mod pinning strategy (OQ6). | Initialize a Module Instance Package from a Published Module |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
